messages.author: a05ad4db1ef329a2
messages.subject: Issue creating large microclimate maps
parts:
Hey all,

As people may remember from previous posts I am looping through to generate microclimates for a large area in the Appalachian mountains.  My issue is that when I generate my resulting rasters from all of my sites, there are normally fairly noticeable transitions between sites, specifically, I can see the outlines of the  ~4-km climate grids for micro_usa despite using ~1-km terrain data.  I know I have seen papers where the maps are much smoother.  

I have included the lapse correction and I have run with the global aerosol database, both on and off, and neither seems to help this issue (the lapse correction obviously helps, but is not alleviating the issue).  

Is there are 1-km climate data set that any of the microclimate models can pull from?  Should I be using a more location-specific lapse correction? Are people applying smoothing calculations to their rasters?  Am I am missing something obvious? I have attached an example image so you can see what I mean.  It is not awful, in my opinion, but certainly noticeable and not ideal. I mostly just want to know what I am doing wrong/differently.

Thoughts?

Vinny

messages.author: e46cb5dd353b7dfb
messages.subject: Re: Issue creating large microclimate maps
parts:
Hi Vinny,

If the lapse-rate correction is working properly, I'm guessing the cloud and perhaps the rainfall are what is causing the 4km pixels to show. My only suggestion is to separately smooth the gridded data beforehand (except the air temps which you should lapse-rate correct). But how are you doing the lapse correction? You should pass the 1 km terrain value for elevation into the model (input parameter 'elev') and then it will adjust with the lapse rate relationship you've specified (or the default one if you haven't specified a lapse rate via parameters 'lapse_max' and 'lapse_min').

All the best,
Mike

messages.subject: Re: Issue creating large microclimate maps
parts:
Hi Mike,

Yep, I have been passing my elevation into elev and I also have the slope, aspect, and 24 horizon layers as well.  I am using the default lapse rates currently.  I am assuming it is working because back when I was using micro_global from version 1 before the lapse rate was included I saw much more distinct separation with the large global grids before I added the lapse corrections.

I guess I was concerned I was not doing something very obvious.  

Your primary suggestion (besides confirming the lapse correction is working) would be to download the corresponding climate data (minus temp variables ) and smooth those rasters and pass them through to the micro_usa function instead of having them taken from opendap? Is there an easy way to include climate data from a local source without extensively editing the function?

Let me know if you can, thanks either way!

messages.author: e46cb5dd353b7dfb
messages.subject: Re: Issue creating large microclimate maps
parts:
Hi Vinny,

There's an input option called 'spatial' for which you can put the folder with the gridMET files and the associated DEM. When 'opendap' is not set to '1', it will look there for them. You could run it this way and put smoothed versions of the grids into that folder, making them otherwise identical in structure and file name, and that should do the trick (but you could crop to your area of interest so they aren't so big).

Also, to double check whether the pixelation is really due to the rainfall/cloud influence, you could run a small area with 'clearsky' set to 1 and the soil moisture model turned off. Then I think it should not look so blocky if the lapse-rate correction is doing its job.

All the best,
Mike
